overview: The Medford School Committee reviewed public health protocols and listened to extensive public comment regarding the extension of the school mask mandate through March 14. The committee also approved a high school mosaic mural project, received updates on math enrichment programs, and voted on fee increases and voucher policy changes for before and after school care.

items.title: Superintendent's Report
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent shared updates on student accomplishments, foundation scholarships, athletic achievements, Black History Month celebrations, and a student event supporting Ukraine.

items.title: COVID-19 Operational and Health Update
items.summary: District officials detailed extending the local mask mandate to March 14 and transitioning from pool testing to rapid home testing kits, followed by extensive public comment from residents and parents.

items.title: Approval of Medford High School Mosaic Mural
items.summary: Principal D'Alleva and Marie Cassidy presented a proposal for a removable mosaic mural installation at Medford High School, which was approved.

items.title: Elementary Math After-School Tutoring Enrichment Program
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Galusi presented an after-school math skill-building program for elementary students using ESSER funds.

items.title: Secondary Education Grant Updates
items.summary: Dr. Cushing reported on a confirmed financial literacy grant and an applied grant to support an April vacation math academy for middle and high school students.

items.title: Before and After School Care Fee Schedules and Policies
items.summary: The committee voted to discontinue accepting state EEC vouchers after the 2021-2022 school year and approved proposed tuition rate increases and policy changes for the 2022-2023 school year.

items.title: Presentations of the Public
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn read the meeting guidelines for public presentations; no public presentations were offered.

items.title: Motion on Medford High School Bathroom Closures
items.summary: Member Ruseau raised concerns regarding bathroom access at Medford High School, prompting administration to outline plans for improved communication and opening additional facilities as lunch operations normalize.

items.title: Condolences
items.summary: The committee expressed condolences to the families of several community members, former staff, and relatives of school personnel.
